title: Safety profile comparison of chimeric live attenuated and Vero cell-derived inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccines through an active surveillance system in Australia.
ehr_evidence: Data were retrieved from SmartVax (www.smartvax.com.au), an active surveillance system for monitoring vaccine safety utilized by more than 450 clinics and other immunization providers.
summary: In a retrospective active surveillance study of 2756 patients receiving either the chimeric live attenuated JE vaccine (Imojev) or the Vero cell-derived inactivated JE vaccine (JEspect) at Australian primary care and travel medicine clinics, overall, systemic, and local adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) were compared between the two vaccines.
key_findings: Overall (7.0%), systemic (2.8%), and local (1.9%) AEFIs were uncommon and not significantly different between Imojev and JEspect (overall OR = 1.27; 95%CI: 0.91–1.77; systemic OR = 1.23; 95%CI: 0.74–2.06; local OR = 1.20; 95%CI: 0.65–2.22).
Patients aged <5 years had higher odds of overall AEFI (OR = 2.39; 95%CI: 1.10–5.19) and local AEFI (OR = 4.13; 95%CI: 1.08–15.74) compared to those aged >50 years.
There was a non-significant trend of differential effect by sex and number of concomitant vaccines, with odds of AEFI increasing in females as the number of vaccines increased.

In the sensitivity analysis restricted to patients who received only a JE vaccine (n = 637), odds of AEFI with Imojev were higher than JEspect but not statistically significant (overall OR = 2.16, 95%CI 0.93–5.01; systemic OR = 3.27, 95%CI 0.73–14.67; local OR = 1.98, 95%CI 0.22–17.87).
captured_features: number of other vaccines received on the same encounter
specific AEFI symptoms (tiredness, headache, fever, irritability, sleep disturbance, diarrhea, vomiting, rigors, convulsions, hypotonia, pain, swelling, rash)
time to onset of AEFI post-immunization
pathologies_diseases: adverse events following immunization (AEFIs) - overall, systemic, and local
study_design: retrospective active surveillance cohort study comparing two vaccines
population: 2756 patients (median age 34 years, IQR 22–51; 52.6% female) receiving Imojev (n = 1855) or JEspect (n = 901) at Australian primary health-care centers and specialist travel medicine clinics, 2015–2020
limitations: Small sample size in children aged <5 years (n = 64), limiting subgroup analysis.
Severity of AEFIs was not recorded in the system.
Only 3–5 day follow-up via SMS, missing late-onset AEFIs (e.g. cardiovascular or neurologic complications).
Self-reported AEFIs with potential age-dependent reporting bias.
Small subgroups prevented analysis of specific vaccine combinations by sex.
